physicalNotes: Radius 1.63 (+0.23/-0.20) Earth radii from Jenkins et al. 2015 (AJ 150, 56 (2015); arXiv:1507.06723), at 6378.137 km per Earth radius. No mass is measured, so no gravitational parameter is adopted. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.shape: Inclination 89.806 degrees from Jenkins et al. 2015, Table 3. The scaled distance a/R* = 202.63 is DERIVED here from their semimajor axis 1.046 AU and stellar radius 1.11 solar radii, not quoted. Jenkins et al. 2015, Table 3, leave the eccentricity unconstrained (e cos omega = 0.03 +0.75/-0.39, e sin omega = -0.02 +/- 0.31; no radial-velocity detection), so the orbit is drawn circular.
sources.phase: Jenkins et al. 2015, Table 3: epoch BJD 2454833 + 314.985.
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
